findings.title: Fireworks October 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: On October 6, 2026, Fireworks identified unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials that gave a third party access to environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts. Fireworks began containment the same day, notified affected customers beginning October 7, rotated employee API keys on October 9, and published this bulletin on October 9 at 10pm PDT. At the time, Fireworks stated it had not detected evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic within its security perimeter.

findings.title: Fireworks Cyberattack Exposes Customer Data And AI Models As Fallout Widens
findings.summary_md: Forbes reported on November 9, 2026 that Fireworks AI, which counts roughly 10,000 enterprise customers including Uber, Salesforce, and others, suffered a cyberattack exposing customer data and model weights, with two customers telling Forbes they had already moved their business off Fireworks systems. The report notes Fireworks disclosed the October incident on October 9 and a subsequent cloud-provider compromise on October 23 that led to additional customer data impact. The article frames a compromise at Fireworks as potentially exposing information of its customers, making the vendor an attractive target.

findings.title: Update on October 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: This update, published November 9, 2026, revises the October 6 incident: after the initial bulletin, Fireworks discovered impacts to account and billing information and, for a limited set of accounts, to secrets, datasets, and incomplete models. The evidence links the activity to a financially motivated threat actor group engaged in LLMJacking, selling tokens from unauthorized access to large language models to illicit routing gateways. Separately, a third-party cloud provider hosting Fireworks R&D machines suffered an incident on October 23, and on October 24 the unauthorized party used it to reach Fireworks development machines and run an unauthorized workload causing additional customer data impact; Fireworks detected this on the same day and remediated.

findings.title: Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack
findings.summary_md: AI infrastructure startup Fireworks disclosed a new security breach in which attackers accessed its development machines after breaching a third-party cloud provider. The company had earlier notified law enforcement and customers of an October incident in which attackers accessed environment variables containing API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts. The follow-on compromise, detected on October 24, involved an unauthorized workload on Fireworks development machines and led to additional customer data impact.

findings.title: Fireworks AI Confirms Wider Breach Affecting Customer Datasets, Model Weights and Notion AI Chats
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported on November 10, 2026 that Fireworks AI's investigation into a security incident first reported in early October uncovered further malicious activity affecting account and billing information, alongside secrets, datasets, and incomplete models for a limited set of accounts. The attackers reached Fireworks' development environment via an unnamed third-party cloud provider that hosted its R&D machines on October 23, 2026, then ran an unauthorized workload on October 24 that led to additional customer data impact. Notion disclosed that the incident impacted fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces, and Fireworks stated payment card numbers are not stored by the company and were not impacted.

findings.title: Uber confirms hackers stole thousands of drivers' license information in data breach
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported on November 13, 2026 that Uber confirmed hackers stole driver's license information for thousands of US drivers during an October breach at Fireworks AI, a third-party AI cloud provider that held Uber records. In notices filed with several US attorneys general, including California, Uber said it was notified by the provider on October 9 that hackers had broken in and stolen internal credentials, and that it determined on October 13 that personal information had been accessed. Uber severed its data connections with the provider and began notifying affected drivers.
